metadata.author: Greg Paskal
metadata.description: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) header missing finding template with comprehensive guidance for all audiences including framework-specific implementation code, testing strategies, and infrastructure deployment procedures for preventing protocol downgrade attacks.

EXECUTIVE.summary: Your website lacks HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) headers, allowing attackers to force users' connections to downgrade from secure HTTPS to insecure HTTP, exposing sensitive data to interception.
EXECUTIVE.businessRisk: Man-in-the-middle attacks can intercept customer credentials, payment information, and personal data. SSL-stripping attacks bypass HTTPS protection. Brand reputation damage from security incidents. Potential compliance violations (PCI-DSS, GDPR) with fines up to 4% of annual revenue or $100,000+ per incident.
EXECUTIVE.complianceImpact: PCI-DSS 4.1 requires HSTS for payment processing. SOC 2 Type II requires transport security controls. GDPR Article 32 requires appropriate security measures. Missing HSTS may trigger mandatory breach notifications and regulatory audits.

PROJECT_MANAGER.summary: Missing HSTS header allows protocol downgrade attacks where attackers force connections from HTTPS to HTTP, bypassing encryption and exposing user data.
PROJECT_MANAGER.timeline: Low implementation complexity but high security impact. Can be deployed within current sprint without blocking other work. Requires coordination with infrastructure team for server configuration changes.
PROJECT_MANAGER.effort: 1-2 hours total: 30 minutes implementation, 30 minutes testing, 30 minutes deployment verification across all environments
dependencies: Ability to test header changes in staging

DEVELOPER.summary: HSTS header instructs browsers to only connect via HTTPS for a specified duration, preventing protocol downgrade and SSL-stripping attacks.
DEVELOPER.technical: The Strict-Transport-Security HTTP response header tells browsers to automatically upgrade all HTTP requests to HTTPS and refuse connections that don't use valid TLS. Format: Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload. Without HSTS, the first request to a site over HTTP is vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks before the redirect to HTTPS occurs.
DEVELOPER.vulnerability: Protocol downgrade attack (CWE-319). Attackers on the network path can intercept the initial HTTP request and prevent the redirect to HTTPS, forcing all subsequent traffic to remain unencrypted. SSL-stripping tools automate this attack. Users clicking http:// links or typing domain names without https:// are vulnerable.

SECURITY_ENGINEER.summary: Missing HSTS enables protocol downgrade attacks, allowing man-in-the-middle interception of initial HTTP connections before HTTPS redirect.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.vulnerability: Protocol downgrade vulnerability (CWE-319, CWE-523). SSL-stripping attacks intercept HTTP traffic and prevent HTTPS upgrade. Browser's first connection to site is vulnerable even if server redirects to HTTPS. Network attackers can inject malicious content or steal session tokens during unencrypted initial connection.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.attackVector: Attacker positions on network path (public WiFi, compromised router, ISP-level). When user visits site via HTTP (typed domain, bookmark, http:// link), attacker intercepts request and proxies connection, stripping HTTPS and presenting HTTP to user while maintaining HTTPS to server. User sees normal site but all traffic is readable by attacker.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.threatLevel: HIGH - Active exploitation common on public networks. Automated tools (SSLstrip, BetterCAP) make attacks trivial. Users on public WiFi, hotels, airports, coffee shops are high-risk. 40% of users type domains without https://, exposing themselves to first-request vulnerability.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.mitigationUrgency: Immediate (within 24 hours). Deploy HSTS with minimum 6-month max-age. Implement across all subdomains. Consider HSTS preloading for maximum protection. One-time configuration with lasting protection.

OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.summary: HSTS header missing from server response configuration, allowing protocol downgrade attacks on production web servers.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.technical: Server (Nginx, Apache, IIS, CDN) not configured to send Strict-Transport-Security header. All HTTPS responses should include this header to instruct browsers to enforce HTTPS-only connections. Configuration is at web server or load balancer level, not application code.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.scope: All web servers, load balancers, reverse proxies, and CDN configurations serving HTTPS traffic. Applies to primary domain and all subdomains if includeSubDomains directive used. Must be configured at outermost edge of infrastructure (CDN or load balancer) to protect all traffic.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.monitoring: Verify HSTS header presence in production using curl or browser DevTools. Monitor for certificate expiration (HSTS with expired cert causes hard failure). Track HSTS max-age to ensure it doesn't expire. Alert on any HTTPS→HTTP downgrade attempts (shouldn't occur with HSTS). Test with SSL Labs for HSTS validation.

QA_TESTER.summary: Missing HSTS header means automated security tests will fail and protocol downgrade vulnerabilities remain undetected until penetration testing.
QA_TESTER.testImplication: Security scanning tools (OWASP ZAP, Burp Suite) will flag missing HSTS as HIGH severity. Compliance tests will fail. Cannot verify SSL-stripping protection. Manual testing required to confirm HTTPS enforcement. Browser DevTools won't show HSTS activation without header.
QA_TESTER.riskIfNotFixed: Security audit failures. PCI-DSS compliance testing blocked. Penetration testers will demonstrate protocol downgrade attacks. User data exposed during testing on unsecured networks. Cannot certify transport security requirements met.

asp-net-core.dependencies:
// No additional packages required
// Built into ASP.NET Core

verificationSteps: 1. Deploy changes to staging/test environment
2. Open browser DevTools (F12) → Network tab
3. Navigate to your site (ensure HTTPS)
4. Click any request → Response Headers section
5. Verify 'Strict-Transport-Security' header present
6. Confirm value: 'max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload'
7. Test in multiple browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
8. Use curl to verify: curl -I https://yourdomain.com | grep -i strict
9. Verify SSL Labs test: https://www.ssllabs.com/ssltest/
10. Check Security Headers: https://securityheaders.com/
11. Clear browser cache and re-test (ensure header persists)
12. Test subdomain if using includeSubDomains directive

nginx.reload:
# Test configuration syntax
sudo nginx -t

# Reload Nginx (no downtime)
sudo nginx -s reload

# OR restart Nginx service
sudo systemctl reload nginx

# Verify process
sudo systemctl status nginx
nginx.verify:
# Verify HSTS header is present
curl -I https://yourdomain.com | grep -i strict-transport-security

# Expected output:
# Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload

apache.config:
# Apache Configuration
# File: /etc/apache2/sites-available/000-default-ssl.conf or httpd.conf

<VirtualHost *:443>
    ServerName yourdomain.com
    
    # SSL Configuration
    SSLEngine on
    SSLCertificateFile /path/to/certificate.crt
    SSLCertificateKeyFile /path/to/private.key
    
    # HSTS Header (only in SSL virtual host)
    Header always set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload"
</VirtualHost>

# HTTP to HTTPS Redirect
<VirtualHost *:80>
    ServerName yourdomain.com
    Redirect permanent / https://yourdomain.com/
</VirtualHost>
apache.enable:
# Enable required Apache modules
sudo a2enmod ssl
sudo a2enmod headers
sudo a2enmod rewrite

# Enable SSL site
sudo a2ensite 000-default-ssl

# Test configuration
sudo apache2ctl configtest

# Reload Apache
sudo systemctl reload apache2
apache.verify:
# Verify HSTS header
curl -I https://yourdomain.com | grep -i strict-transport-security

# Check Apache error logs if issues
sudo tail -f /var/log/apache2/error.log

cloudflare.config:
# Cloudflare Dashboard Configuration
# 1. Log into Cloudflare dashboard
# 2. Select your domain
# 3. Navigate to: SSL/TLS → Edge Certificates
# 4. Scroll to 'HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS)'
# 5. Click 'Enable HSTS'
# 6. Configure settings:
#    - Status: On
#    - Max-Age: 12 months (31536000 seconds)
#    - Apply HSTS to subdomains: Yes
#    - Preload: Yes (if ready for HSTS preload list)
#    - No-Sniff Header: Yes
# 7. Read and acknowledge the warning
# 8. Click 'Save'

# Note: Ensure valid SSL certificate is active before enabling HSTS
# Cloudflare will automatically add the header to all HTTPS responses
cloudflare.verify:
# Verify through Cloudflare dashboard or curl
curl -I https://yourdomain.com | grep -i strict-transport-security

# Expected output:
strict-transport-security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload

aws-elb.config:
# AWS Application Load Balancer - Add HSTS header
# Using AWS CLI:

aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn <listener-arn> \
  --default-actions Type=forward,TargetGroupArn=<target-group-arn> \
  --alpn-policy HTTP2Preferred

# Add custom header using Lambda@Edge or CloudFront:
# 1. Create Lambda function to add HSTS header
# 2. Associate with CloudFront distribution
# 3. Or configure in ALB target group attributes

# Alternative: Configure at application level (recommended)
# See Developer framework examples above
aws-elb.verify:
# Test from outside AWS
curl -I https://yourdomain.com | grep -i strict

# Check ALB logs in S3 or CloudWatch

verificationSteps: 1. Test configuration syntax before applying changes
2. Apply changes to staging environment first
3. Verify HSTS header with curl: curl -I https://yourdomain.com
4. Test in browser DevTools → Network tab → Response Headers
5. Validate with SSL Labs: https://www.ssllabs.com/ssltest/
6. Check Security Headers: https://securityheaders.com/
7. Test subdomain access if using includeSubDomains
8. Monitor error logs for any issues
9. Verify across all environments (dev, staging, prod)
10. Document change in change management system
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.rollbackPlan:
1. Comment out HSTS header line in configuration file
2. Reload/restart web server
3. Verify header removed with curl
4. Note: Browsers cache HSTS for max-age duration
5. Users may need to clear browser HSTS cache manually
6. Chrome: chrome://net-internals/#hsts → Delete domain
7. Firefox: Delete site-specific settings
8. Rollback should be avoided - only if certificate invalid

manualTests.name: HSTS Header Presence Test
steps: 2. Press F12 to open Developer Tools
5. Click on the document request (usually first in list)
manualTests.expected: Header 'Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload' is present in all HTTPS responses

manualTests.name: HTTP to HTTPS Redirect Test
steps: 1. Type http://yourdomain.com in browser address bar
4. Check address bar after page loads
6. Check Network tab for redirect chain
7. Verify 301 or 302 redirect from HTTP to HTTPS
manualTests.expected: Browser automatically redirects from http:// to https:// and HSTS header enforces HTTPS-only connections

manualTests.name: Subdomain HSTS Inheritance Test
steps: 2. Check Developer Tools → Network → Response Headers
3. Verify HSTS header present on subdomain
manualTests.expected: If 'includeSubDomains' directive used, all subdomains inherit HSTS policy and enforce HTTPS

edgeCases: Test on different browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
Test on mobile devices (iOS Safari, Android Chrome)
Verify behavior with expired SSL certificate (should fail hard)
Test with self-signed certificate in development
Verify HSTS preload list inclusion (if preload directive used)
Test behavior after max-age expiration (requires time manipulation)
Verify HSTS works with CDN (Cloudflare, Akamai, Fastly)
Test subdomain access with and without includeSubDomains
Verify HSTS survives browser cache clear
Test with browser HSTS cache manipulation (chrome://net-internals/#hsts)
